paper_sections.title: Brain activation patterns associated with cue reactivity and craving in abstinent problem gamblers, heavy smokers and healthy controls: an fMRI study
Results for performance data and craving ratings
Correlations between BOLD activation, subjective craving, BDI-II and CAARS

description.value: The study compared fMRI cue reactivity to gambling, smoking-related, neutral and low-level baseline pictures in treatment-seeking problem gamblers, heavy smokers and healthy controls, and examined associations between cue-related brain activation and subjective craving.

design.value: A functional magnetic resonance imaging event-related cue reactivity paradigm was used in 17 treatment-seeking non-smoking problem gamblers, 18 non-gambling heavy smokers and 17 non-gambling and non-smoking healthy controls. Group differences and regression associations with craving were examined using second-level random-effects analyses.

task_description.value: A picture two-choice response task presented 30 gambling pictures, 30 smoking-related pictures, 30 neutral pictures and 30 low-level baseline pictures randomly, with no more than three pictures of the same stimulus category in a row. Each picture was presented for 5 seconds, followed by a 2.5-second blank screen. The scanning session lasted 15 minutes and each gambling, smoking-related and neutral picture was presented once.

instructions.value: For gambling, smoking-related and neutral pictures, participants pressed a response button with the left index finger when a face was present and the right index finger when no face was present. For low-level baseline pictures with arrows pointing left or right, participants gave the corresponding left or right response. Participants were requested to respond within 5 seconds and were not encouraged to respond as quickly as possible.

stimuli.value: Gambling, smoking-related, neutral and low-level baseline pictures. Pictures were matched for complexity, naturalistic setting, sex of people depicted and neutral facial expressions.

task_performance_measures.value: Mean reaction time to the pictures in each stimulus category

modality.value: T2*-weighted echo planar images sensitive to blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) contrast

instrument.value: 3.0 Tesla Philips Intera full-body fMRI scanner equipped with a standard SENSE RF head coil (Quasar gradient system, Philips Medical Systems BV, Eindhoven, the Netherlands)

description.value: During the task, T2*-weighted echo planar images covering the entire brain except for the inferior regions of the cerebellum were acquired with 35 axial slices, a 0.3 mm interslice gap, a 64 × 64 mm matrix and 90 kHz bandwidth.

instrument.value: 3.0 Tesla Philips Intera full-body fMRI scanner

description.value: A sagittal T1-weighted structural scan was acquired for co-registration with the fMRI data.

Images were slice-timed, reoriented and realigned to the first volume. T1-coregistered volumes were normalized to an SPM T1 template using 12 linear parameters and nonlinear cosine basis functions, followed by spatial smoothing with an 8 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.

software.value: SPM2 (Statistical Parametric Mapping; Wellcome Department of Cognitive Neurology, London, UK)

steps.value: Normalization to an SPM T1 template using 12 linear parameters and a set of nonlinear cosine basis functions
Spatial smoothing using an 8 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel

model_settings.value: Delta functions convolved with a synthetic hemodynamic response function were used to model responses to each stimulus type.

For each comparison of interest, single-subject contrast images were entered into second-level random-effects analyses. One-way ANOVAs and interaction effects were used for gambling versus neutral pictures in PRG versus HC or HSM and for smoking-related versus neutral pictures in HSM groups versus PRG or HC. Group interactions were reported with a cluster size restriction of 5 voxels at P < 0.001, masked with the appropriate main effect. Main and interaction effects were reported with a cluster size restriction of 10 voxels at P < 0.05 corrected for multiple comparisons according to the Family Wise Error method.
